title: LFO RND page
author: MrScruff (rytm-mods); elemod port: Iced-Cream
description: A second LFO page, LFO RND, reached by pressing the LFO page key again: two random modifiers per sound, each a destination (DS1/DS2, one of 16, chosen from stock's LFO DST list) and a depth (DP1/DP2, 0..64 in 16 steps). On every note trig each modifier draws a random offset for its destination, clamped to the parameter's range, held until the next note, on top of p-locks, slides and LFO 1. Stored in the sound through core-ar2 0.2's mod storage (one 16-bit sound field), so the sound's stock bytes stay stock; sounds saved by lfo-rnd 1.0 keep their settings. Port of rytm-mods 0004-lfo-rnd. From 1.2 the page goes through core-ar2 0.4's page tables and page-key lists (needs core 0.4, OS 1.74 only). From 1.3 (core-ar2 0.9) the four settings are four 4-bit sound fields, each a lockable parameter registered in core_lock_params on its page knob: DS1 and DS2 are lockable (p-locks, scene locks, MIDI) and step without smoothing; DP1 and DP2 are also LFO, velocity and aftertouch destinations (RND:Random 1 Depth, RND:Random 2 Depth). At each note's start the audio interrupt takes the four as core plays them (core_param_int: the sound's value, the trig's p-lock or the scene's lock, plus the performances, the LFO and the routes), so a p-locked or modulated depth or destination draws that note's offset. Settings saved by 1.1 and 1.2 (one 16-bit field) load as the defaults; lfo-rnd 1.0's word still loads (needs core 0.9). From 1.4 (core-ar2 0.13) the page's four knobs are the mod's own knob ids ("knobs": 4) in place of stock ids 1..4: no stock parameter record is patched, DS1 and DS2 draw as stock's LFO DST knob and DP1 and DP2 as a dial through core_knob_looks, and the knob draw site at 0x400a85e8, which core-ar2 0.13 takes, is gone, so it links with core-ar2 0.13 and later, flashed and from the +Drive (needs core 0.13). From 1.5 (core-ar2 0.17) DS1 and DS2 open the destination list through core_knob_flags entries, and the open list's knob is core's core_knob_list_id: the four sites 1.4 gated for the list flag (0x40039d94, 0x40039fbe, 0x4003a224, 0x4003a890) are core's, and the destination list's commit is taken in the parameter class's apply, where it stops for an own id (0x400a9e2a), in place of the setter's entry, which core-ar2 0.17 takes for ev_param_set; so 1.5 links with core-ar2 0.17 and later (needs core 0.17).
